rationale: Task T5 requires class prevalence with counts and imbalance, a flagged-vs-unflagged feature comparison restricted to legitimately available, non-label-derived claim-level fields, and an explicit leakage assessment. Plan: load_tables (row/column counts, and the manifest already shows the claims->members join is m:1 with match_rate 1.0 and 0 unmatched keys), class_prevalence (positives/negatives/total, prevalence, imbalance ratio; produces fraud_prevalence.png), feature_comparison on 13 claim-level features covering type/coding/setting/provider/network categoricals and cost/utilisation numerics plus claim flags (produces fraud_comparison.csv). Deliberately excluded: fraud_pattern_type (label-derived; it is non-null on 647 rows = exactly the positive class, so it encodes the label), member_sex, member_race_ethnicity and member_age_band (protected attributes), and member_payer_type (member-level demographic/socioeconomic proxy, not a claim-level feature). leakage_assessment is switched on (it is off by default) so the report names label-derived, identifier and protected fields and confirms none appear in the comparison. write_report prints every rate as numerator/denominator, cites an artifact or metrics key for every result, and includes the synthetic-data, descriptive-only, association-not-causation, class-imbalance, small-groups (the positive class is roughly 5% of 12,845 claims, so categorical cells within it will be small) and no-operational-use caveats; sample_preview and model_limitations are omitted because no sampling or modelling occurs.
